Enel Generacion Peru SAA Announces Major Investment to Expand Renewable Energy Capacity

LIMA, Peru – Enel Generacion Peru SAA, one of the country’s leading electric utilities, announced on Tuesday a significant investment plan aimed at expanding its renewable energy generation portfolio over the next three years, underscoring the company’s commitment to Peru’s energy transition and growing electricity demand.

The Lima-based utility said it will allocate approximately $240 million to the development and enhancement of solar and hydroelectric facilities across several regions, with the objective of increasing its installed renewable capacity by 20% by the end of 2027. The investment is expected to boost local job creation, support national decarbonization targets, and enhance energy security.

“Peru’s energy landscape is evolving, and we are proud to help drive that transformation,” said Andrea Conti, CEO of Enel Generacion Peru SAA, during a press conference. “Our investment will not only expand clean energy capacity, but also deliver tangible benefits to the communities where we operate, in line with our sustainability commitments.”

The expansion will focus on upgrading existing hydroelectric plants in the Junín and Cusco regions, as well as constructing a new 110 MW solar park in the Arequipa area. The company expects construction work to commence in the fourth quarter of 2024, subject to regulatory approvals.

According to industry analysts, Enel Generacion Peru SAA’s move comes at a time of rising electricity demand in Peru, driven by economic recovery, industrial growth, and population increases. “This investment positions Enel Generacion Peru SAA as a key player in Peru’s clean energy future,” said Samuel Vega, energy sector analyst at Capital Insights Peru. “It aligns with the government’s ambition to achieve 60% renewable energy generation by 2030.”

Local trade groups welcomed the announcement, highlighting the potential economic and social impact. The Peruvian Association of Renewable Energy Producers noted that the initiative could create up to 1,200 direct and indirect jobs during construction and operation phases. “We see this as a major step forward for regional development and skills training,” said association president Luz Romero.

The Peruvian government has set ambitious targets to reduce carbon emissions and increase the share of renewables in the national energy mix. The Ministry of Energy and Mines recently streamlined permitting for clean energy projects, a move Conti cited as crucial for the company’s expansion plans.

Enel Generacion Peru SAA reported a 7% increase in net profit in its most recent financial results, reflecting stable demand and operational efficiencies. The company’s shares rose 2.3% on the Lima Stock Exchange following the investment announcement.

Conti said the utility remains open to further partnerships with local suppliers and communities as it implements its expansion roadmap. “We are committed to sustainable growth and to supporting Peru’s long-term energy needs,” she said.
